result.summary: Implemented docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md exactly as designed, no schema change (confirmed: registrations.event_id/admission/created_at/id and registrations_waitlist_order_idx already existed from REQ-011; DATA-DESIGNER correctly not dispatched). New export in apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts: getWaitlistPosition(db, eventId, registrationId) implementing §2.2 literally -- one SELECT ... LIMIT 1 for the target row's created_at/admission (returns null if not found, defensive per §2.2 step 1), a second null-return if the row's admission is not currently 'waitlisted' (§2.2 step 2), otherwise one SELECT of ids matching event_id + admission='waitlisted' + the 'ahead' condition (created_at earlier, OR created_at equal AND id lower -- §2.3's tie-break), with the result being that count + 1 (§2.2 step 4). Built with plain Drizzle eq/lt/and/or (imported lt/or newly, eq/and reused) -- no raw SQL, no window function, no ORDER BY/LIMIT-based ranking -- matching the filter shape of registrations_waitlist_order_idx (event_id, created_at) WHERE admission='waitlisted'. Zero writes anywhere in the function; no interface anywhere in this file or RegistrationOutcome/RegisterForEventResult gained a position/rank field. decideRegistrationOutcome and registerForEvent are untouched (byte-identical to REQ-020, confirmed by diff -- this design's own explicit reuse decision, §9). Handler wiring in apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts: inside the existing display-data-fetch conditional (unchanged block for admitted/waitlisted/already-registered), one new call to getWaitlistPosition only when outcome.kind==='waitlisted', threaded into composeRegistrationReply as a new waitlistPosition:number|null parameter (default null, so admitted/already-registered/refusal call sites are unaffected). composeRegistrationReply's waitlisted case now builds an ordered line list -- waitlistedPrefix, eventTitle, dateTimeText, then (only if waitlistPosition!==null) a position line built as `${waitlistedPositionPrefix} ${position}`, then waitlistedWhatNext unconditionally -- exactly per §3.2, with §3.1's chosen null-handling (silent omission, no placeholder/error text). i18n additions in apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts: two new Catalog.registration keys, waitlistedPositionPrefix and waitlistedWhatNext, added to all three files in one edit each (parity discipline) -- ru/en given placeholder copy per decisions/0002, with waitlistedWhatNext deliberately avoiding any specific auto-promotion timing/mechanism claim per §6 open question 2's flagged caution (REQ-023 auto-promotion is not yet built). catalogs.test.ts required no change (its own generic parity/non-empty check covers the new keys automatically) -- confirmed green. New tests: apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts gained two new describes (4 new cases) -- 'getWaitlistPosition REQ-021 AC2' (the exact §0-specified recipe: 3 waitlisted rows with strictly increasing created_at inserted directly, position for the 2nd confirmed =2, a raw `pool.query("UPDATE registrations SET admission='withdrawn' WHERE id=$1", ...)` against ONLY the 1st row -- never through any application function, since no withdraw feature exists -- then the 2nd row's own updated_at re-read and asserted byte-identical, and its position re-read and confirmed =1; plus two defensive-case tests for a non-waitlisted row and an unknown id, both returning null) and 'registerForEvent REQ-021 AC4' (1 admitted + 6 waitlisted registrations against a capacity=1 event, every waitlisted call returns kind='waitlisted' with zero refusal, and the last-inserted row's own computed position equals the full count of 6, proving the ranking still holds at this size). New file apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.test.ts (2 cases) -- AC1, exercised through a real grammY dispatch (bot.handleUpdate(), same api.config.use-capturing-transformer pattern as handlers/start.test.ts, real migrated scratch Postgres): a registration against a fully-booked (capacity=1, pre-filled) published event replies with a message containing waitlistedPrefix, 'waitlistedPositionPrefix 1', and waitlistedWhatNext; a second registrant against the same event gets position 2. AC verification, all against a real scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, migrated via drizzle-kit migrate): AC1 PASS -- handlers/registration.test.ts's two cases confirm the waitlisted confirmation message states a computed position (1, then 2 for the next registrant) via a live bot.handleUpdate() dispatch, not a mock. AC2 PASS -- registration.db.test.ts's dedicated case: position for the 2nd of 3 waitlisted rows read as 2, a direct SQL admission flip of ONLY the 1st row's admission column (no application-level withdraw call, none exists), the 2nd row's own updated_at captured before and after and asserted toEqual (byte-identical, zero write), then getWaitlistPosition re-read for the 2nd row and confirmed =1 -- proving the recompute-on-every-call design by construction. AC3 PASS -- `git grep -niE "waitlist.?(position|rank)" -- apps/bot/src` and a targeted grep of apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts for position/rank find only: two schema.ts comments (documentation, not columns), the unrelated pre-existing profiles.position text column (a person's job title, REQ-019, nothing to do with waitlisting), and every reference being to the getWaitlistPosition function/its call sites/its own tests -- no column, cache, or persisted field anywhere holds a waitlist position or rank; the value exists only as this function's return value, a SELECT count(*) expression over created_at/id. AC4 PASS -- registerForEvent's decideRegistrationOutcome (unchanged) accepted 6 waitlisted registrations past a fully-booked capacity=1 event with zero refusal, confirmed both by outcome.kind on every call and a direct SELECT counting exactly 6 waitlisted rows afterward. Commands run from the REPO ROOT (never --root apps/bot): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings, unchanged). `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces; apps/web Next.js build succeeded, apps/bot's `tsc -p tsconfig.json` clean with zero errors (getWaitlistPosition's new lt/or imports and null-narrowing typecheck cleanly). `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot, required once 2+ DB-backed test files coexist per REQ-020's own recorded issue) -> 16 files / 178 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Re-ran just the two REQ-021-touched files with --reporter=verbose to individually confirm every one of the 19 registration*.test.ts cases (13 pre-existing REQ-020 + 4 new AC2/AC4 cases in registration.db.test.ts + 2 new AC1 cases in the new handlers/registration.test.ts) actually executed against the live Postgres rather than silently skipping -- all 19 green. 178 = REQ-020's own confirmed baseline of 172 + 6 new cases (4 + 2) added by this run. Scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432) was started fresh for this run (was not already running) and left running for REVIEWER/TEST-RUNNER's convenience -- not torn down. `git status --porcelain` confirms only the 6 modified files + 1 new file listed in artifacts_out are dirty.

docker exec bot-postgres-1 pg_isready -U bot -> accepting connections
DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx drizzle-kit migrate -> migrations applied successfully
npm run lint (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web warnings)
npm run build (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces, apps/bot tsc clean
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root) -> 16 files / 178 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

same command scoped to apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts + apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.test.ts --reporter verbose -> 19/19 passed, all individually confirmed executed (not skipped) against the live scratch Postgres, including the AC2 updated_at-unchanged assertion
git grep -niE "waitlist.?(position|rank)" -- apps/bot/src -> only function/test references to getWaitlistPosition, no stored field
git grep -niE "position|rank" -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts -> only doc comments and the pre-existing unrelated profiles.position (job title) column
git status --porcelain -> only the 6 modified files + 1 new file listed in artifacts_out are dirty

ac_results.AC1: PASS -- a live bot.handleUpdate() dispatch against a fully-booked event replies with a message stating waitlistedPositionPrefix + '1' for the first waitlisted registrant and + '2' for the next one, confirmed via handlers/registration.test.ts (real grammY dispatch, no mock of the handler itself)
ac_results.AC2: PASS -- with 3 waitlisted rows, a direct SQL flip of the 1st row's admission column (no withdraw feature exists) changes the 2nd row's getWaitlistPosition result 2->1 on the next call, while the 2nd row's own updated_at is captured before/after and asserted byte-identical (toEqual), proving zero write to that row
ac_results.AC3: PASS -- git grep across apps/bot/src for any position/rank column, cache, or persisted field finds nothing beyond the getWaitlistPosition function itself and its call sites/tests, plus one unrelated pre-existing profiles.position (job title) column; the waitlist position is a query expression over created_at/id, never stored
ac_results.AC4: PASS -- 6 registrations past a fully-booked capacity=1 event all return kind='waitlisted' with zero refusal, confirmed by both outcome.kind and a direct COUNT of waitlisted rows
